A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe ConlangCrafter with matching authors, methods, and applications. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated between sections.

before.justification: v1 reports original quantitative comparisons using three base LLMs, component ablations, and qualitative examples of generated languages in Section 3.

after.justification: v2 reports original quantitative comparisons, expanded ablations, generated-language examples, and expert–automatic agreement results on 200 translations.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains the same language-sketch bootstrapping, constructive translation, randomness injection, and critic–editor self-refinement pipeline. The stopping rule of a score of at least 9 or ten iterations moves from v1 Appendix A.1 to v2 Section 3.1; no procedural change is established.

E1.justification: Both versions cover unconditional and user-constrained conlang generation and the same ten English-to-conlang translation sentences. The sixteen WALS features and qualitative scenarios are retained. The expert evaluation assesses outputs within this existing coverage.

E2.justification: The main comparison retains the single-prompt baseline under the same three base LLMs. Within the ablation comparison, v2 Table 3 adds a separately evaluated multi-hop-only (+MH) condition absent from v1 Table 2; retained RNG and self-refinement stages receive more explicit labels.

E3.justification: v2 removes the separate sketch-consistency evaluation based on fifteen sampled statements per language, retaining translation consistency. It adds expert scoring of 200 translations on a three-level scale. Section 3.1 also revises the stated language count from twenty to fifteen–twenty-one depending on setting, although table captions still say twenty. These reported changes do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds an expert–automatic agreement and calibration analysis, testing the validity of translation judging, and expands the ablation to isolate multi-hop reasoning separately from randomness injection. These address evaluator reliability and component contributions beyond v1's RNG/self-refinement ablation. The qualitative case studies are retained.

E5.justification: The main and ablation tables switch from reporting standard deviations to standard errors. v2 additionally introduces Spearman correlation and quadratic weighted kappa with significance tests for expert–automatic agreement, which v1 did not report. Neither change establishes an increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: Comparing v1 Table 1 with v2 Table 2, ConlangCrafter diversity values change from 0.32/0.37/0.35 to 0.60/0.59/0.57 for Gemini Flash, Gemini Pro, and DeepSeek-R1. Pro translation consistency changes from 0.39 to 0.44 and DeepSeek-R1 from 0.32 to 0.35. Sketch-consistency results disappear; multi-hop-only and expert-agreement results are added, including rho = 0.515 and kappa = 0.304. Revised sampling descriptions prevent treating these as matched-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: The language-sketch notation, pairwise Hamming-distance formulation, and translation-consistency ratio remain unchanged. Neither version supplies theoretical propositions or proofs. Removing the standard proportion formula for sketch consistency accompanies the dropped empirical metric rather than a change in mathematical reasoning.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain end-to-end conlang generation through modular prompting, randomness injection and self-refinement, constructive translation, optional user control, and automatic evaluation. The added expert check supports the retained evaluation contribution; wording changes in the abstract and conclusion do not redefine the scientific claims.

C2.justification: v2 newly interprets automatic judgments as stricter than expert ratings but moderately aligned with them. It explicitly notes that binary consistency scoring penalizes minor and major errors equally and that fully consistent translation remains challenging. The component interpretation now discusses multi-hop reasoning, while most applicability limits remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a full annotation protocol in Appendix A.3, specifying materials, scoring, LLM hints, and treatment of invented rules and independent translations. It also documents annotator qualifications and format-based rejection sampling. Existing decoding and self-refinement settings are relocated. The revised missing-feature description no longer explicitly states v1's rule excluding unspecified WALS values.

R1.justification: Section 4 retains the same cited works and positioning against piecemeal conlang tools and single-prompt language generation. The bibliography contains the same works; differences are formatting and pagination.

P1.justification: v2 tightens several method paragraphs and the conclusion, adds a manual-evaluation subsection and annotation appendix, and moves implementation and WALS explanations into the main text. It also removes the acknowledgments. The overall section sequence and narrative remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 is redrawn with different t-SNE positions and visual styling. The WALS table moves from appendix Table 5 to main-text Table 1. Quantitative tables lose the sketch-consistency row, gain an explicit MH ablation column, and revise labels and captions. The qualitative displays, pipeline illustration, and two-column layout are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 improves component analysis and documents a 200-translation expert check, but the annotator saw the automatic judgments being validated, limiting independent corroboration. It also removes direct sketch-consistency evidence, where the Gemini variants had underperformed the baseline, and substantially changes scores without reconciling the revised sample counts with table captions. The added checks and lost evidence create material tradeoffs whose net effect on paper quality cannot be reliably determined.
